title: Bristol Trainers, look to the stars: Minior returns for the Leonids Meteor Shower!

content:
The night sky is about to get a little more interesting for Pokémon GO trainers, and Bristol players have another reason to grab their phones and head outdoors. As the annual Leonids meteor shower approaches, Pokémon GO is bringing back Minior Showers, giving trainers another opportunity to encounter the colorful Rock- and Flying-type Pokémon Minior in the wild.

The event runs from Saturday, November 14, at 5:00 p.m. through Thursday, Nov. 19, at 11:59 p.m. During the event, shooting stars will illuminate the in-game sky between 5 p.m. and 9 p.m. each evening, bringing an increased chance of encountering Minior. Trainers looking to build their Stardust collection, there’s an especially attractive bonus: every Minior caught during the event will award 1,000 Stardust.

A Colorful Pokémon With a Mystery at Its Core

Minior is one of Pokémon GO’s more unusual encounters. It has seven different core colors: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, and Violet. Each of the six scheduled meteor showers will introduce a different core color. Green Core Minior made its debut during the October Orionids event, but the core color scheduled to debut during the Leonids has not yet been announced. That means trainers will have another opportunity to expand their Minior collections while keeping an eye out for the next color reveal.

Understanding Minior’s Two Forms

Minior isn’t just an interesting addition to a collection. It also has a unique battle mechanic. Minior begins battles in Meteor Form, where it has higher Defense but lower Attack. Once its health drops below 50%, it changes form and exposes its core. In its exposed-core form, Minior trades some of its defensive strength for increased Attack. Initially, this transformation will only occur when battling Team GO Rocket, team leaders or in the GO Battle League.

Bristol Trainers: Where to Play

For local trainers, the evening hours offer a great opportunity to get outside, explore Bristol, and enjoy the event together. Consider making a few stops around town:

  • Memorial Boulevard: A familiar destination for trainers looking to walk, explore, and check nearby Pokémon activity.
  • Bristol City Hall Clocktower: A convenient downtown meeting point for local players.
  • Muzzy Field: Another familiar stop that can be incorporated into an evening Pokémon GO outing.
  • Page Park: A great option for trainers looking to enjoy an outdoor walk while playing.
  • Bristol Public Library and downtown: An opportunity to combine a little exploration with checking PokéStops and nearby spawns.

Remember that Minior’s increased encounter window runs from 5 p.m. until 9 p.m. each day. Plan your walks accordingly!

Quick Event Guide

Minior Showers: Leonids 2026

Starts: Saturday, Nov. 14, at 5 p.m.  Ends: Thursday, Nov. 19, at 11:59 p.m. Special Feature: Shooting stars appear in the in-game sky during the evening hours.

  • New Core Color: To be announced.
  • Featured Pokémon: Minior (Meteor Form)
  • Stardust Bonus: 1,000 Stardust per Minior caught
  • Increased Encounter Window: 5 p.m.–9 p.m. daily

Tips for Trainers

A few things to keep in mind before heading out:

  • Save your Stardust opportunities: With 1,000 Stardust awarded for every Minior caught, this is a great opportunity to build your resources.
  • Play during the evening window: The increased Minior encounter chance makes 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. the most important time to get outside.
  • Bring plenty of Poké Balls: Make sure your item bag is ready for an evening of catching.
  • Explore with friends: Bring other trainers along and make an evening of exploring Bristol.
  • Keep an eye on core colors: The Leonids are another step in the ongoing Minior color releases, so watch for announcements about the next debut.

The Stars Are Just Getting Started

The Leonids event also arrives during an exciting weekend for Pokémon GO. Nov. 14 and 15 mark the dates for Pokémon GO Wild Area 2026: Global, bringing Steel- and Dragon-type adventures, powerful Pokémon, and new Dynamax and Gigantamax encounters. With Minior showers beginning Saturday evening, Bristol trainers will have plenty of reasons to stay active in Pokémon GO throughout the weekend. Whether you’re hunting for Stardust, searching for a new Minior core color, or simply enjoying the game with friends, the Leonids offer another reason to look up at the virtual night sky.

The stars are falling, and Minior is waiting! head Into the Wild!
